events.continuity_hook: Continues the narrowed DC family episode after Maya's spouse confirmed the school-break travel window.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the flight-and-hotel pairing, identify the booking path, and note any remaining seat or hotel-rate details before purchase.
events.scenario_brief: Maya is ready to commit to the family Washington, DC spring-break trip for Friday, April 4 through Tuesday, April 8 after a final fare check. They want to leave Atlanta after school without arriving too late, keep the Tuesday return in the early-to-mid afternoon, avoid connections unless the savings are large, and choose a hotel that works for three people with easy Metro access and a simple breakfast plan. The remaining decision is whether to pay more for the most convenient nonstop into DCA and a cancellable Metro-adjacent hotel, or accept a less convenient airport or prepaid hotel rate to keep the total cost down.

events.continuity_hook: Pre-trip follow-up for the already-booked DC spring-break trip.
events.interaction_goal: Assess the schedule change, decide whether to keep the flight, and check the practical hotel and seating details before departure.
events.scenario_brief: Two days before the DC family trip, Maya checks the itinerary after the airline moves the Friday outbound earlier by about half an hour. The family still needs to get from school pickup to ATL without rushing, keep seats together if possible, and confirm that the hotel will hold bags and that breakfast hours fit early museum starts. The unresolved item is whether the earlier flight is still workable or whether a later nonstop into a different DC-area airport is worth the tradeoff.

events.continuity_hook: New work-travel episode after the DC family trip is complete.
events.interaction_goal: Frame the trip, identify viable flight windows and hotel areas, and call out what must be confirmed before booking.
events.scenario_brief: Maya begins planning a solo client rollout trip from Atlanta to the Raleigh-Durham area for Tuesday, May 6 through Friday, May 9, with meetings expected near Cary. She needs simple flights from ATL, ideally arriving Monday evening early enough to review materials and returning Friday afternoon after a planned morning wrap-up. The hotel should be a short rideshare from the client site, have strong guest reviews, and make breakfast and dinner easy during long workdays. The client has not yet confirmed the exact office address or whether the Friday wrap-up will end before noon.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Raleigh client rollout episode after the office location and first meeting time are confirmed.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the flight tradeoffs and select the itinerary Maya should submit for approval, with seat selection noted if it cannot be handled immediately.
events.scenario_brief: The client confirms the Cary office address and an 8:30 a.m. Tuesday start, and Maya needs to route the flights for approval before the end of the week. A nonstop Delta itinerary from ATL to RDU fits the schedule well, while a cheaper one-stop option saves money but adds connection risk and pushes the arrival later. For the return, the best afternoon nonstop is available but has limited seat selection, and an earlier flight may be too tight if the client wrap-up runs long.

events.continuity_hook: Follows the Raleigh flight decision and shifts the episode to lodging near the confirmed client site.
events.interaction_goal: Build a concise hotel comparison, choose the best booking candidate, and keep a backup option in case the rate changes before approval.
events.scenario_brief: With the Raleigh flights selected, Maya now needs a three-night hotel near the Cary client office. She wants a quiet room suitable for evening work, a customer rating around 4.0 or better, breakfast if practical, and nearby dinner options so she does not need a rental car. The two strongest options split the priorities: one is closer to the client and has an on-site restaurant but no clear free breakfast, while the other has breakfast and a suite-style room but is a longer rideshare.

events.continuity_hook: Late itinerary adjustment in the Raleigh client rollout episode after the client changes the meeting agenda.
events.interaction_goal: Evaluate the schedule risk, compare the return-flight and hotel-change options, and identify the safest plan before travel starts.
events.scenario_brief: The day before the Raleigh departure, the client adds a late Thursday stakeholder session that may run past the original airport-transfer window. Maya needs to decide whether to keep the Friday afternoon return as planned, shift to a later evening flight, or add one more hotel night and return Saturday morning. She wants the fare difference and hotel-change impact separated clearly, and she also needs to confirm late checkout or luggage storage if the Thursday schedule remains extended. The main unresolved issue is whether the client agenda is firm enough to justify changing the return now.
